title: Big Ideas, Big Changes: Meet Lingo and the Inventions
bigQuestion: How do inventions change our lives?

maya.name: Maya
maya.persona: cheerful 10-year-old girl, curious and full of questions

leo.name: Leo
leo.persona: friendly 10-year-old boy, loves building and fixing things

focusWords.kidDefinition: A new thing that people make for the first time.
examples: The telephone was an amazing invention.
Every invention starts with one good idea.

focusWords.kidDefinition: A round part that turns, so things can roll.
examples: Round wheels help cars and bikes move easily.
My toy truck has four wheels that spin.

focusWords.kidDefinition: A vehicle with two wheels that you pedal.
examples: I ride my bicycle to school every morning.
Maya fixed her bicycle with her dad this weekend.

focusWords.kidDefinition: A big boat that carries people or things across the sea.
examples: The big ship sailed across the sea to Crete.
Many ships carry food and toys to other countries.

focusWords.kidDefinition: A machine that you use to work, play and learn.
examples: My computer helps me learn English every day.
Leo uses the computer to build robots online.

focusWords.kidDefinition: Facts or news that help you learn about something.
examples: The library has lots of information about dinosaurs.
Can you find information about bicycles for our project?

focusWords.kidDefinition: A small brush you use to clean your teeth.
examples: Please take your toothbrush on the school trip.
Brush your teeth with a toothbrush every morning and night.

focusWords.kidDefinition: A liquid soap you use to wash your hair.
examples: She washed her hair with a new shampoo.
This shampoo smells like oranges and feels very soft.

lines.text: Hoo hoo! Welcome to our new unit, everybody. I am Lingo.
Today, Maya and Leo are going to show us something surprising.
Leo says that a tiny idea can change the whole world!
Maya says that the wheel is the best invention ever made.

question.text: What is one thing in your home that you think is a great invention?

prompt.text: Point to the picture of a big boat that carries people or things across the sea.

explain.text: A ship is a big boat that sails across the sea.

prompt.text: Listen to the word: computer. Which picture matches it?

explain.text: A computer is a machine we use to work, play and learn.

prompt.text: We ride our ____ to the park every Saturday.

explain.text: A bicycle has two wheels, and you pedal it to go places.

prompt.text: Clean your teeth with a ____ every morning.

explain.text: You clean your teeth with a toothbrush every morning.

prompt.text: She washed her hair with a new ____.

explain.text: Shampoo is a liquid soap that we use to wash our hair.

prompt.text: A wheel is a round part that helps things roll.

explain.text: Wheels turn round and round, so cars and bikes can move.

prompt.text: An invention is a new thing that people make for the first time.

explain.text: An invention is something new that helps people, like the telephone.

prompt.text: Which word is the odd one out?

explain.text: Bicycle, ship and wheel are about moving, but a toothbrush is for cleaning teeth.

prompt.text: Can you give me some ____ about trains, please?

explain.text: Information means facts that help you learn about something.

lines.text: Now let's play memory. Turn two cards and find matching pairs.
Say each word aloud as you turn the card. Good luck!

prompt.text: Tell your partner about an invention that you use every day.

frames: I think the ___ is a very important invention.
I use a ___ every day because it helps me.
Without a ___, my life would be very different.

model.text: I think the computer is a very important invention. I use a computer every day because it helps me learn. Without a computer, my life would be very different.

lines.text: Wonderful work, everyone! You met eight Big Question words today.
From the wheel to the computer, inventions change our lives every day.
Next time, we will read about Maya and Leo and their weather cat!

exitTicket.text: Name one invention from today's words and say why it is useful.
Where can you find information about a new invention?
